testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does blocking a load do?

options.text: It is dangerous and should never be done.
It keeps the load from moving.
It is only used with liquid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps the load from moving.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from shifting while you are driving.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: What affects how far a vehicle travels before stopping?
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass and leave more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops and prevents a crash. Speeding up will make things more dangerous.

questions.question: In a vehicle with a manual transmission, how do you prevent rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake to prevent rolling backward. Use the parking brake if needed.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which belt do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt. Look for cracks, frays, and that they are tight. If any parts are not belt-driven, tell the examiner.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are called headache racks. They protect the driver if cargo moves during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be seen as:
questions.explanation: Talking to passengers takes attention away from driving. Be extra careful around distracted drivers.

questions.question: Livestock being transported can:

options.text: Never be transported on a trailer.
Only be transported after a police inspection.
Move and shift, making the vehicle harder to control.
Only be transported by registered farmers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move and shift, making the vehicle harder to control.
questions.explanation: Livestock moves and shifts its weight while being transported. This makes the vehicle unsafe and harder to handle.

questions.question: When asked to make a turn on the driving test, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal because you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.

questions.explanation: Always check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal when making a turn.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil that build up over time. Not draining them can damage the system. Open manual drains at the end of each day.

questions.question: What should you do when parked on the side of the road?

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use only one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you park on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed on a wet road?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when the road is wet because tires have less grip. Slow down by about one-third of your normal speed.

questions.question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens more easily when tire pressure is low or tread is worn. Good tire tread helps water drain away. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: What condition should engine belts be in?
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. Each belt has a safe amount of movement, so learn what is right for your vehicle.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, or drinking while driving distracts you. Plan ahead and take a break to eat on long trips.

questions.question: How often should you stop to rest on long drives?
questions.explanation: Take a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles to avoid getting too tired.

questions.question: What is the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination should lose no more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from moving or falling during transport.

questions.question: When you must stop before turning during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after the stop line for a better view.
Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line or sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let the vehicle roll. Stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: Which is NOT a type of tie-down equipment?
questions.explanation: Use the proper number of tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Examples include ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in very wet weather when temperatures are below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze so the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.
The brakes may become too smooth to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze so the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in very wet weather when temperatures are below freezing. The brakes could freeze and become locked, making it impossible to move the vehicle.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver:

options.text: May use any cell phone while driving.
May only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
May only use a cell phone while driving on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
questions.explanation: If you use a mobile phone while driving a CMV, you may only use a hands-free phone placed close to you. Even hands-free phones can distract you from driving. Know all cell phone laws in your state.

questions.question: Which vehicle does NOT have an exemption from the CDL requirement?
questions.explanation: A CDL is not required to drive military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, or recreational vehicles. It is also not required for a straight truck carrying only your personal property that you are not selling.

questions.question: What can extremely hot temperatures cause?
questions.explanation: Air expands when hot, so tire pressure increases in hot weather. This can cause tire failure. Check your tire pressure regularly on hot weather trips.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for tires on the back of a CMV?
questions.explanation: Check tire tread depth in every major groove. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch. Back tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The number of alcoholic drinks consumed
How quickly the alcoholic drinks were consumed

questions.explanation: Three main factors determine BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it is consumed, and the person's weight.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a driver who might be a hazard?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without first scraping ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
The driver of a station wagon with items covering the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. Examples include drivers with ice on windshields, those driving vehicles with large items blocking windows, and those unfamiliar with a rental truck's limited rear visibility.

questions.question: The parking brake should be:

options.text: Used whenever you park your vehicle.
Set when driving in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used whenever you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve goes between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from leaking out of the system if the compressor breaks.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance for air brake vehicles has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, a pull-up happens when you stop and pull forward to get a better position. Stopping without moving forward is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: When should you downshift?
questions.explanation: You must downshift before going down a hill or entering a curve.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: On vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), a yellow warning light tells the driver that the ABS is not working.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, how often must drivers check that it is secure?
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure within the first 50 miles of your trip. Then check it again every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Can radial and bias-ply tires be used together?

options.text: Yes, but only on the rear axle
No, they should not be used together

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, make sure radial and bias-ply tires are not being used at the same time.

questions.question: If you plan to stop on the road to unload cargo, you should:

options.text: Stop suddenly since you are already on the road
Tap your brakes to warn other drivers
Wave your arm out the window to get attention

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes to warn other drivers
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your brake lights to warn other drivers whenever you slow down or stop where they may not expect it. Do this when you stop on the road to unload cargo or passengers.

questions.question: About height warnings on low bridges:

options.text: They must be posted at least twice
They may be posted, but are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be posted, but are not required
questions.explanation: Height warnings are often posted on low bridges, but not always. If you are not sure if you can clear an overhead object, drive slowly.

questions.question: When checking tires during a pre-trip inspection, you should look at the:
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tire pressure is not too low or too high.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel as hard as possible.

questions.explanation: When your vehicle hydroplanes, do not hit the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle, which of these is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust system parts rubbing against fuel system parts.
Exhaust system parts that are leaking.
Exhaust system parts made of aluminum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts made of aluminum.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the exhaust system, look for loose, broken, or missing parts; loose or missing brackets and bolts; parts rubbing against other parts; and leaks. The material of the exhaust parts is not a concern.

questions.question: How can you reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress can lead to aggressive and dangerous driving. Playing calming music helps you relax while driving.

questions.question: In cold weather, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: In cold weather, bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Be extra careful when driving on bridges and overpasses in cold, wet conditions.

questions.question: What could reduce the space between the road and an overhead object like a bridge?
questions.explanation: Bridge height signs may not be exact. If the road was repaved after the sign was installed, or if snow is on the ground, the clearance will be different than the sign shows.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting your trip. If your vehicle has a trailer, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What should air tank drains do?

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the air tanks in an air brake system. Always drain the tanks completely.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, make sure the header board is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to contain cargo.

questions.question: What must be done if a load is longer than allowed?

options.text: A warning flag must be placed on the end of the load.
The load may only be transported between 6 p.m. and 3 a.m.
The emergency flashers must be activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning flag must be placed on the end of the load.
questions.explanation: Oversized loads need special equipment like warning flags or flashing lights. You must get permits for such loads. Driving times may also be limited.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should move no more than:
questions.explanation: To check slack adjusters, park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and release the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster. It should not move more than one inch. If it moves more, it needs adjustment.
